what_happened: Job 20261105-051400-dzr4 ("Refuse bug-fix readings that lack a root-cause criterion and real-data", class of work: code) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 5 of 5 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic confirmed the fix location (a new `step!` in `refusing_check`, modelled on `check_code_survey`), the demonstration seams, the dependents list and the budget-set placement. One major finding remained: the cue classifier for "this is a bug-fix request" is unsound. Family (i)'s copula guard barely constrains anything because nearly every sentence has a copula. Matching per line misfires both ways when requests put whole paragraphs on one line. The creation-word exemption includes the adjective "new", so real feature wording in CHANGELOG.md still matches. The round-5 claim that this was fixed does not hold. Two minor findings: family (ii) matches the common "Fix newcomer gaps on the X page" shape with no corpus case deciding it, and whether the cited class is caught depends on the opening verb, which the doc comment does not say. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The plan designed a text classifier (cue families, copula guard, exemption words, per-line unit) from the reading's wording and a few hand-picked cases. Nothing makes planning run the draft rules over the real corpus of past requests and changelog lines, which are paragraph-length lines, before the critic sees them. So false matches show up only as critic judgment, one finding at a time. Five fixed rounds keep no partial plan and have no repair step. A defect that could be measured by running the matcher on real text instead takes all rounds and then loses the whole planning spend. The rule also decides pass or fail through the replay hold, so classifier looseness directly sets the job's outcome.
prevention: Before a plan for a new refusal or matching rule goes to the critic, run a check that applies the plan's draft matcher to every request and changelog entry in the repo's refusal corpus and records the matched and refused counts and examples. The plan is sent back mechanically if the match rate on known ordinary non-bug-fix text is above a set bound, or if it matches text from the repo's own changelog. The matcher also works per sentence by default, with a required copula right before the error word and the exemption limited to a sentence's leading verb. A purely measurable defect then fails fast and cheaply instead of at round 5.
proposed_request: Add a refusal for bug-fix readings that lack a root-cause criterion and a real-data criterion, and make it precise enough not to refuse ordinary feature work. Outcome: when the request (including the original request of a retried attempt, so "try again on <id>" is covered) describes fixing wrong output or behavior, a reading that has no criterion naming the root cause and no criterion that runs against real data is refused, and the refusal text says what to add. Detect bug-fix requests per sentence, not per line, because requests often put a whole paragraph on one line. Require a copula directly before the error word. Apply the creation-word exemption only to a sentence's leading verb. Do not count "new" as an exemption word. Acceptance: (1) a corpus test lists real past requests and CHANGELOG.md lines (including lines 311 and 3076), each marked refuse or accept, and the test fails on the base tree for the refuse cases; (2) "Fix newcomer gaps on the X page" has a corpus case that decides it; (3) "Show only ..." and "Make ... show only ..." have corpus cases and the doc comment states which opening verbs are caught; (4) the replay over past real requests refuses no ordinary non-bug-fix request, and the refusal is declared intended with the replay share measured; (5) the steward re-check and `check_reading_text` both go through the same check; (6) the size and count assertions in briefs.rs and the changelog are updated. Keep it to this one rule; do not change other readers.
